# @ternent/ledger

> A signed, append-only history of JSON entries, verified on open.

Three exports from the package root: `createLedger`, `openLedger`, `createWriter`.
Types: `History`, `Writer`, `Commit`, `Entry`, `EntryInput`, `Json`, `JsonObject`,
`Signer`, `Relationship`. Declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`.

```ts
import { createIdentity } from "@ternent/identity";
import { createLedger, createWriter, openLedger } from "@ternent/ledger";

const alice = await createIdentity();
let history = await createLedger({ signer: alice });
const writer = createWriter(history, alice);
writer.append({ kind: "note.added", payload: { text: "hello" } });
history = await writer.commit();

const reopened = await openLedger(history.export());
const entries = reopened.commits.flatMap((commit) => commit.entries);
```

- Histories are immutable and only come from Ledger. Don't build or spread one.
- Read entries from `history.commits[i].entries`. The signer is `commit.proof.signer`;
  the claimed time is `commit.proof.createdAt`. Put event time in your payload if needed.
- Ledger keeps no derived state. Reduce entries into your own state.
- `writer.commit()` rejects if nothing is staged, and on failure keeps the staged entries.
  Don't call `append`, `discard` or `commit` while a commit is pending; they throw.
- Decide in your app whether a signer may write. Ledger only proves who signed.
- `openLedger` accepts only canonical bytes from `export()`. Store and send those bytes as-is.
- One limit: `maxBytes` (default 16 MiB) on `createLedger` and `openLedger`.
- Values must be JSON with safe integers only: no floats, `undefined`, `Date` or class instances.
- Errors are ordinary `Error`/`TypeError`/`RangeError` with a message; there are no codes.
